prompt: Full-color outdoor photograph taken at eye level in the afternoon, with low sunlight coming from frame-right and casting long shadows across a neighborhood park. In the center, a white man in his thirties with fair skin, short brown hair, and light stubble walks along a paved path while holding a medium-sized golden retriever on a dark green leash. He wears a faded blue overshirt over a grey T-shirt, tan trousers, and worn brown walking shoes. His body faces left as he takes a step forward, looking down toward the dog with a neutral expression. The leash hangs in a loose curve between his right hand and the dog’s red collar. The golden retriever walks beside him on the left, its cream-gold coat lit along the back and ears, head lowered toward the grass and tail raised behind it. Dry leaves and small twigs lie near the edge of the path in the foreground. On the right, the sun sits just above the line of trees, producing a bright patch of glare and warm highlights on the man’s sleeve and the dog’s fur. Behind them, an open lawn extends toward scattered shrubs and mature tree trunks, with a wooden bench resting near the path. In the background, muted brick houses and parked cars form simple shapes beyond the foliage, while the pale blue sky occupies a narrow band above the treetops.

Full-color indoor large-format photograph in a vertical 4-by-5 composition, showing the interior of a brutalist concrete church from a low, wide-angle viewpoint. Massive raw concrete walls rise around a cavernous nave, their surfaces marked by formwork seams, pinholes, chipped corners, and broad geometric planes. In the upper center, a narrow rectangular opening cuts through the thick wall as one slot of hard daylight falls diagonally into the otherwise dark sanctuary. The bright beam forms a single pale shaft across the center, revealing suspended dust particles against deep grey-brown shadow. One empty wooden pew stands alone within the light, placed off-center in the lower middle of the frame and facing the unseen altar beyond it. Its long plank seat has a dull brown finish, worn edges, visible grain, and two heavy supports; the backrest is bare, with no person or object resting on it. Behind the pew, the concrete architecture expands into angular buttresses and an overhanging ceiling slab that disappears into darkness. On the left, a recessed wall remains nearly black, while the right side contains a massive cantilevered concrete volume with a rough aggregate texture. At the far end, the daylight slot ends at a small altar-like projection of unadorned concrete, but its details remain lost in shadow. The floor consists of broad poured-concrete slabs with hairline joints and scattered grit. The concentrated beam illuminates only the pew and a thin patch of floor beneath it, leaving the surrounding nave in dense shadow.

Studio fashion photograph captured on a Hasselblad medium-format camera, full-length portrait against an unmarked mustard seamless paper backdrop. A Black female model in her twenties with dark skin and a tall, slender build stands just left of center, facing the camera with her body turned a few degrees toward frame-left. Her short natural hair is cropped close to the head, leaving the oversized grey wool coat as the dominant form. The heavy coat falls below her knees in broad, boxy folds, with dropped shoulders, wide sleeves, a high folded collar, concealed front closure, and two deep patch pockets. Both hands are tucked into the pockets, pulling the lower front into angular pleats. Her face has a neutral expression, closed lips, and a direct gaze. One hard key light from the upper left strikes her forehead, cheek, shoulder, and the raised ridges of the wool, producing bright highlights along the left side while the right side falls into dense charcoal-grey shade. A crisp-edged shadow extends behind her across the mustard paper toward the lower right, following the silhouette of the coat and legs. Dark straight trousers and black leather ankle boots emerge beneath the hem. The seamless paper curves into the floor without a horizon line, its matte surface showing fine tonal falloff around the sharp cast shadow. The composition contains only the model, coat, footwear, mustard background, and shadow, with clean negative space above and to the right.

Traditional Japanese woodblock print in the Hiroshige register, rendered entirely in indigo and sumi ink on warm off-white washi paper with visible fibers and uneven carved edges. A broad wooden bridge crosses a rushing river from the lower left toward the center-right, its dark timber planks and low railings reduced to crisp, rhythmic lines. Sudden rain fills the upper half of the composition as dense, fine parallel indigo lines slanting diagonally across the entire scene. Above the bridge, layered blue-grey storm clouds sweep over distant mountains, their flattened silhouettes breaking into pale mist and deep indigo cloud bands. In the foreground, three small travelers stand close together beneath umbrellas on the bridge: one figure in a dark robe holds a round indigo umbrella, another carries a black umbrella, and a third wears a muted grey cloak beneath a smaller umbrella. Their bodies lean forward against the downpour, with hems and sleeves bending in the wind. Below them, white water surges around the bridge supports in curling sumi waves marked by sparse indigo foam crests. On the left bank, reeds and wet grasses rise beside a cluster of dark rocks; on the right, a windswept pine bends over the riverbank. The restrained composition uses broad areas of untouched paper, flat color separations, irregular hand-printed registration, and no lettering, seals, captions, or decorative inscriptions anywhere.

Studio product photograph of a cylindrical tea tin against a seamless warm grey background, shot from a slightly elevated three-quarter angle with hard side light entering from the left. The tin stands upright in the center, its front facing the viewer and its right side receding into shadow. Its body is coated in dark green enamel with a narrow gold rim around the top and bottom edges. A fitted dark green lid sits flush above the body, edged by a thin gold band; the raised metal lid knob catches a bright highlight while the right half falls into deep shade. Across the upper front, large embossed gold serif capitals read "HIGHLAND BREAKFAST". Directly beneath, smaller gold lettering reads "Assam and Ceylon leaf". Below it, a circular gold roundel contains the text "est. 1884" in compact dark green type. On the visible right side of the tin, small white sans-serif lettering follows the curve of the cylinder and reads "Brew for four minutes. One spoon per cup and one for the pot." The hard light creates a sharp vertical highlight along the left edge, reveals the enamel’s smooth reflective surface, and casts a dense shadow behind and to the right of the tin. A few tiny scuffs interrupt the green finish near the lower rim, and the tin rests on a matte tabletop with a short, crisp cast shadow extending toward the lower right.

Studio photograph of a letterpress gig poster printed on thick cream paper stock, shown straight-on against a plain neutral background with even, shadowless lighting.
